{"caption":"My apartment runs itself, and this one is everything that happens while I am asleep.

Shades close at 9:22. Kitchen shelf lights shut off at 9:50, which is my signal that the day is over. The Pura kicks on lavender. My Eight Sleep adjusts the bed temperature all night based on my body. The humidifier holds the room at 60%. And 45 minutes after sunrise the blackout layer opens first, then the solar shades, so I wake up to the skyline instead of an alarm.

I set all of it up once and it has run every night since. That is the whole point of the hometel.

Save this for when you are ready to automate your own space and send it to whoever you share a bed with.

#smarthome #homeautomation #hometel #eightsleep #sleeproutine","likes":78258,"comments":371,"photoCount":0,"videoCoverCount":1}

{"caption":"My apartment basically runs itself, and I’m not exaggerating.

These are the 4 things doing my chores for me: Easyplants that water themselves, a Roomba that cleans my floors on a schedule (and spot-cleans any mess from the app), a Pura that keeps my place smelling like a 5-star resort on a timer, and smart plugs that run all my lights so they’re on at sunset and off by 10. This is how I keep a small apartment feeling like a hotel without actually doing the work every day. Small space, fully automated. 

Save this for when you set up your own space, and send it to whoever’s apartment never feels finished.

#smartapartment #apartmentliving #smallspaceliving #smarthome","likes":15081,"comments":67,"photoCount":0,"videoCoverCount":1}

From a full five star luxury experience at the Equinox Hotel to the aesthetic rooftop vibes at PUBLIC to the boutique communal energy at Arlo, there is something here for every type of traveler. And if you book Arlo, use code TYLERlCRAWFORD for up to 40% off your stay.

{"caption":"Apple HomeView. $299, ships November 13.

It sits on your counter or mounts to your wall and runs your whole home. Basically the control panel from a nice hotel suite, except it also handles your music and your calls.

Three things that stood out to me. It recognizes up to six people by face and voice and switches to their content automatically, and none of that data leaves the device. The Home Camera face streams up to nine camera feeds at once, and it listens for your smoke and CO detectors and pings your phone if one goes off. And it hands off from your iPhone mid podcast or mid recipe so you pick up right where you left off in the kitchen.

Worth knowing: Siri AI on it is in beta, English only at launch, and the wall mount, cable, and power adapter are sold separately.

I bought one. Full review once it ships.

Save this if you’re deciding. Follow for the real test.

#applehomeview #smarthome #apple #hometech #smarthomeideas","likes":384,"comments":38,"photoCount":0,"videoCoverCount":1}

{"caption":"Two years in Hometel 1.0 and today is my last day. 617 square feet taught me a lot, and these are the three I’d pass on.

Plan your layout before you move anything heavy, because rearranging a sofa four times is not a personality trait.

Do smart shades on day one, light control is the difference between a dorm and a suite.

If it doesn’t have a home before you buy it, don’t buy it.

Hometel 2.0 starts soon.

Save this for your next move. Send it to whoever just signed a lease.

#movingtips #smallspaceliving #apartmenttherapy #firstapartment #apartmentdesign","likes":426,"comments":33,"photoCount":0,"videoCoverCount":1}

{"caption":"The thing nobody tells you is that every room has the same views and the same access to the gym, which is 60,000 square feet and the largest Equinox ever built. You are not paying for a better room. You are paying for more space.

My pick is the Deluxe One Bedroom Suite. Separate living area, real desk, and it lands well under the Premier suites for what you actually get.

One note on the Sleep Lab. It is a package you add to a Premier King, not something the room comes with. Worth knowing before you book.

Premier King in November. Follow for the rest of the eight.

Save this before your next New York trip.

#equinoxhotel #hudsonyards #nychotels #hotelreview #nyctravel","likes":156,"comments":4,"photoCount":0,"videoCoverCount":1}

{"caption":"Two years on the 55th floor. Five things I did not know before I signed.

The fire alarm system is compartmentalized, so floor 40 can alarm while I hear nothing. The elevators run lobby to 55 in forty seconds until rush hour hits. The building sways in high wind and it is supposed to. The $200 amenity fee actually buys something. And the view never turns into background noise, which is the part I was most sure would happen.
Save this for apartment hunting. Send it to whoever keeps saying they want to live in a high rise.

Same room either way. One of them gives the floor back during the day. The other one costs half.

Part two is the decision.

{"caption":"Where to stay in Manhattan, from someone who books these rooms on his own dime.

The Manner in SoHo for something with real character, where the TV arrives in a suitcase if you ask. PUBLIC Hotel in SoHo if you want the most aesthetic room of the four, plus the best rooftop in the neighborhood. Arlo Midtown for the Arlo Suite terrace with three landmarks in one view. And Arlo SoHo for the rooftop and a terrace room of your own.

Swipe for the exact room types I’ve stayed in at each, how to pick between midtown and SoHo, and one booking tip most people forget until it’s too late. Code TYLERCRAWFORD gets you up to 40% off at both Arlo locations.

{"caption":"Planning a holiday trip to Manhattan? Here are my top 4 hotels in the two best neighborhoods to stay in.

In midtown, the Arlo Midtown is my 4 star pick, and the Arlo Suite comes with the largest outdoor terrace I have ever had at a hotel, with views of the Empire State Building, World Trade Center, and Hudson Yards from one spot. Down in SoHo, the Arlo SoHo is the fun one with constant rooftop events, and the City Terrace room gets you private outdoor space. And The Manner is the most unique boutique hotel I have stayed at in Manhattan. The rooms do not come with a TV, but ask for one and it arrives in a suitcase.

{"caption":"I have the 16 Pro, 17 Pro, and 18 Pro, so I shot the same things on all three to figure out who should actually upgrade.

Each year changed a different part of the camera. The 17 Pro was about zoom and selfies, with a zoom lens four times sharper and a front camera that auto-rotates and reframes. The 18 Pro changed none of that. Same zoom lens, same sensor. What’s new is a main camera that physically opens and closes, pulling in about 50 percent more light at night or closing down to keep more of the scene sharp, plus manual control for the first time.

On a 16 Pro, upgrade. You get two years at once. On a 17 Pro, only if you shoot low light or want manual control. And the 16 Pro actually zooms further than both.

Save this before you buy and send it to your friend who upgrades every single year.

#iphone18pro #iphone17pro #appleevent #cameracomparison #techreview","likes":168,"comments":17,"photoCount":0,"videoCoverCount":1}
